newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin likely to be in hospital all week - Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin likely to be in hospital all week - Kremlin.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin is "very likely" to spend the rest of this week in a Moscow hospital where he is undergoing tests ahead of planned heart surgery, Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Tuesday.
He told reporters that doctors would meet on September 25-26 to set the date of Yeltsin's operation.
"It is very likely that Boris Nikolayevich (Yeltsin) will stay in the Central Clinical Hospital until the end of the week," Yastrzhembsky said.

His doctors had said last Thursday, when Yeltsin arrived back in Moscow from his holiday home for a check-up, that they would set the date of the operation between September 27 and 29. Yeltsin went into the elite Central Clinical Hospital on Friday and was first due to spend the weekend, then another two days.

Yastrzhembsky denied rumours that the president's health was deteriorating. The best proof that Yeltsin was in good form was the fact that he met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin for over an hour on Tuesday, he said.
He made no mention of any plans to hand over presidential powers during the operation. Yastrzhembsky said last week Yeltsin was considering various ways of passing on some authority.
